common_name: Frontier Red Azalea (Red-Orange Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Frontier Red is an Aromi hybrid bred from 'Forty-niner' crossed with the Ilam hybrid 'Tintoretto'.

directions: Frontier Red is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid azalea bred from a cross of his own 'Forty-niner' with the New Zealand Ilam hybrid 'Tintoretto', opening into roughly three-inch red-orange flowers flushed bright red with red tubes and a faint orange blotch. It carries forward the bold two-tone coloring of its 'Forty-niner' parent while drawing extra vigor from its Ilam strain heritage, and it later became an important parent itself, used to breed the unscented, deep-red 'Pirate's Booty' and 'Pirate's Pink' as well as the yellow-and-red 'Indian Spring'. The deciduous shrub blooms in a heavy spring flush typical of the Aromi breeding line. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, mulching to protect the shallow root system through Gulf Coast summer heat.

common_name: Moon Dreams Azalea (Fragrant White Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Moon Dreams is an Aromi hybrid bred from his OF-1 selection crossed with 'Centerpiece.'

directions: Moon Dreams is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid azalea from a cross of his OF-1 selection with 'Centerpiece', opening into large, fragrant white flowers set off by a deep yellow blotch. It is one of several white-flowered siblings sharing the same OF-1 x 'Centerpiece' cross, alongside 'High Tide', 'Peach Glow', and 'Pale Moon', each selected for slightly different blotch intensity or petal flush. The deciduous shrub blooms in a heavy spring flush and shares the Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance typical of the Aromi breeding line. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow roots through summer heat.

common_name: Peach Glow Azalea (Light Yellow Native Hybrid Azalea with Red-Orange Flush)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Peach Glow is an Aromi hybrid bred from 'Goldstrike' crossed with 'Centerpiece.' Not to be confused with the unrelated Lantana camara 'Little Lucky Peach Glow.'

directions: Peach Glow is a Dr. Eugene Aromi hybrid azalea bred from a cross of 'Goldstrike' with 'Centerpiece', opening red-orange buds into fragrant light yellow flowers with a red-orange flush along the petal tips. It is a sibling of 'High Tide' and 'Moon Dreams' through its 'Centerpiece' parent, while its 'Goldstrike' side traces back to the austrinum-derived Aromi breeding line. The deciduous shrub produces a heavy spring flush typical of the Aromi breeding line and shares its Gulf Coast heat tolerance. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch well to protect the shallow root system through summer heat.

common_name: Sandra Marie Azalea (Pink Knap Hill Deciduous Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Sandra Marie is a Knap Hill-strain selection raised by Bovees Nursery and later used by Dr. Eugene Aromi as a parent of 'Jubilation.'

directions: Sandra Marie is a Knap Hill-type deciduous azalea raised by Bovees Nursery of Portland, Oregon from a seedling grown from imported Knap Hill Nursery seed of unrecorded parentage, registered in 1961. Each truss carries twelve to fourteen flowers, three and a half to four inches wide, in a light yellowish pink flushed with strong reddish orange and centered with a light orange-yellow blotch, on a slow-growing shrub that reaches roughly five feet after two decades. Dr. Eugene Aromi later used it as the Knap Hill parent crossed with Rhododendron austrinum to produce the fragrant yellow hybrid 'Jubilation.' Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, and mulch to keep the shallow root system cool through summer.
sources: Azalea Society of America plant database
